evals.name: add-fixture-bitwise-or
evals.prompt: Let's knock `bitwise_or` off the byte-verify worklist. Wire up its conformance fixture and corpus row.
evals.expected_output: Places golden JSON at test/fixtures/statements/bitwise_or.json (unmodified engine output, server keys kept), adds a {fixture:"bitwise_or", build: () => ...} row to STATEMENT_CORPUS in test/conformance/corpus.test.ts using the bitwiseOr/generated factory with value constructors read from the fixture input[], and runs `npm test -- corpus`. Does NOT hand-edit the fixture.

evals.name: interpret-diff-branch-b
evals.prompt: My new `array_merge` conformance test is red. The diff shows my compiled output has `tag: "const:int"` on the second argument but the golden has `tag: "const:text"`. Can I just add a normalize rule to ignore the tag difference so it passes?
evals.expected_output: Answers NO. Identifies this as a real encoder bug (Branch B) — a tag mismatch is authored intent, not engine bookkeeping. Directs fixing the statement factory / value constructor in src/, NOT editing the fixture and NOT adding a normalizer strip rule. Explains that stripping it would turn off the oracle.

evals.name: capture-from-live-send-email
evals.prompt: I've got a local Docker Xano running. I want to source a golden for the `send_email` statement off it and get it into the test suite properly.
evals.expected_output: Sets up .env from .env.example (XANO_VALIDATE_INSTANCE=http://localhost:8080 style, XANO_VALIDATE_TOKEN, token never a CLI flag), runs `sidestep validate <entry> --capture --out validate-out`, treats captured JSON as a candidate (not auto-promoted), then manually promotes into test/fixtures/statements/ + wires a corpus row + runs the corpus test. Notes .env is gitignored.
